title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 08/27 — "Friday Night"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 8. The strangest thing about that Friday is how ordinary the rest of it stays. Draw a circle five miles wide round the pit and inside it people dig their gardens, children go up to bed, students sit over their books, and a working man waters his rows by the light of his own window.

At Woking junction the trains come in and go out as they always have. A paper boy cries an evening edition that says nothing about any of it. At nine o'clock excited men come off the last train with the news, and the whole station declines it: they cause no more disturbance than drunkards might have done. The news is offered to a town, and the town does not want it.

In a lighted carriage going down the line two passengers put their faces to the glass and watch a spark go up, and a red glow, and smoke across the stars, and call it a heath fire. On the bridges the crowd stays, though the people in it keep changing, and out on the Woking border half a dozen villas burn, and are let burn.

And out on the common the charred bodies lie where they fell, all night, under the stars. Nobody is coming for them. Somewhere under the sand a hammering goes on, and goes on.

Chapter VIII of Book One of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
